prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Miami for hurricane-rated roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there isn’t one objectively “best” roofing company for hurricane-rated replacements in Miami — the right choice depends on your roof type, budget, warranty needs, and whether the contractor is properly certified for Miami‑Dade/High‑wind installations. I can help you find and vet top local options if you tell me your ZIP code. Meanwhile, here’s a practical guide so you can pick the best contractor for your job.

What to require from any hurricane-rated roofer
- Miami‑Dade approvals (NOA) for materials: materials and assemblies must be Miami‑Dade Notice of Acceptance (NOA) or Florida Product Approval–rated for high winds. Ask for the NOA numbers for the exact product/assembly they plan to use.  
- Proper licensing and insurance: verify their Florida contractor license and current general liability + workers’ comp insurance. Use the Florida DBPR license search to check status.  
- Local permitting and inspections: they must pull permits and arrange final inspections with Miami‑Dade/City building department.  
- Manufacturer certification: prefer installers certified by the shingle/metal manufacturer (e.g., GAF, CertainTeed, Owens Corning, TAMKO, etc.) so you get a full manufacturer warranty.  
- Written, itemized contract: scope, materials, fastening method (nail vs. screw, adhesive, number/type of fasteners), underlayment, flashing details, debris cleanup, timeline, and payment schedule.  
- Warranties: ask for both contractor workmanship warranty and manufacturer product warranty; get both in writing.  
- References and recent work: ask for recent hurricane-rated installations in Miami and check photos/references and online reviews (Google, BBB).

Questions to ask every candidate
- Are the products and installation method Miami‑Dade NOA-approved for our roof type? Can you show NOA numbers?  
- Are you licensed/certified to do hurricane-rated high-wind roofing in Miami? Can I see your license and insurance?  
- Will you pull permits and coordinate inspections?  
- What manufacturer certifications do you have? What warranties are provided?  
- How do you secure the roof to meet wind uplift requirements (e.g., straps, deck attachment, fastener pattern)?  
- Can you provide a written line-item estimate and a schedule?  
- Do you use subcontractors? Are they insured/licensed?  
- How do you handle change orders and lien releases?

Red flags (avoid these contractors)
- Door‑to‑door solicitors right after a storm or pressure to sign immediately.  
- Asks for full payment in cash up front or no written contract.  
- Refuses to pull permits, provide license/insurance, or provide references.  
- Dramatically low bids with vague scope or unclear materials.

Materials and systems commonly used for hurricane-rated roofs
- Impact-rated/NOA-approved asphalt shingles installed per high-wind attachment patterns.  
- Concrete or clay tiles with proper anchoring and clips (installation must meet NOA).  
- Standing-seam metal and thru-fastened metal with manufacturer/Miami‑Dade approvals for high winds.  
- Low-slope: TPO, PVC or modified bitumen systems with manufacturer specs for wind uplift.

Where to verify credentials and reviews
- Miami‑Dade County Building Department / NOA database (Miami‑Dade NOA listings).  
- Florida Department of Business & Professional Regulation (DBPR) license lookup.  
- Better Business Bureau, Google/Yelp, and local homeowner groups (Nextdoor/Facebook).  
- Ask your insurance company for contractors they’ve worked with for hurricane-rated jobs — insurers often know reliable vendors.

If you want specific company names
Provide your ZIP code and I’ll pull together a short list of well‑reviewed, NOA‑knowledgeable Miami roofing contractors and what to verify for each. If you already have bids, you can paste the proposals and I’ll compare them line‑by‑line (materials, fasteners, NOAs, warranties, permit handling).
